blocks.content: The spec field is, quite literally, the desired state covered throughout the Internals module, this topic formalizes exactly what that means in practice, across every different Kind.
1. spec Is the Desired State, Formally
blocks.text: 1. spec Is the Desired State, Formally

blocks.content: This is not just a naming convention, exactly as covered in the Desired State vs Current State topic, spec genuinely is the desired state, the target every relevant controller is continuously working to make true.

blocks.alt: Not just a name, this field genuinely is the desired state covered in the Internals module

blocks.content: 2. The Shape Varies Completely by Kind
blocks.text: 2. The Shape Varies Completely by Kind

blocks.content: A Pod's spec centers on containers, a Service's centers on selector and ports, they share the same field name, but their actual content is entirely different, shaped by what that specific Kind is actually for.

blocks.alt: The same field name, entirely different content, shaped by what each Kind actually represents

blocks.content: A Deployment's spec holds replicas and template (covered in the next topic), a ConfigMap has no spec at all (using data instead, covered below), the shape is always specific to the Kind it belongs to.

blocks.alt: Concrete, real examples of just how differently spec is shaped across Kinds

blocks.content:
# Deployment spec
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template: { ... }

# Service spec
spec:
  selector:
    app: my-app
  ports:
    - port: 80

blocks.content: 4. The One Constant Across Every Kind
blocks.text: 4. The One Constant Across Every Kind

blocks.content: Despite the wildly varying shape, one thing never changes, spec always means "what you want to be true," regardless of which specific Kind you are looking at.

blocks.alt: The one constant, however differently shaped, across every single Kind

blocks.content: ConfigMap and Secret, both covered in the Configuration module, are a genuine exception, they use data instead of spec, since they hold plain configuration values rather than describing a desired behavior to reconcile toward.

blocks.alt: A genuine, real exception, worth knowing rather than assuming spec is truly universal

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: spec genuinely is the desired state covered in the Internals module, its content varies completely by Kind, but it always means "what you want to be true."
ConfigMap and Secret are a real exception, using data instead of spec, worth knowing rather than assuming every single Kind follows the same pattern.
